gap_name: Formal specification language with preconditions/postconditions for ignition functions
supporting_evidence: S120-047 and S120-050 provide machine-checkable refinement types and SMT-based equational verification for pure functional programs. S120-017 and S120-018 use execution/test feedback to validate synthesized programs. S120-007 and S120-001 show neural architectures that induce or compile programs from weak or natural-language supervision.
non_supporting_evidence: No source in the reviewed set provides a formal precondition/postcondition language for neural-weight functions. Refinement types apply to symbolic code, not to weight-space artifacts. PAW and Neural Programmer use natural language or weak supervision, not formal contracts.
revised_assessment: GAP-015 is satisfied for symbolic/functional programs but remains unsatisfied for neural and weight-space functions. The Function OS must either restrict node 1 to symbolic specifications or develop a new refinement logic for weight-space artifacts. Current confidence: MEDIUM-LOW.
readjudication_status_reason: Mapped from 121 partial/fulltext review to allowed status taxonomy.

gap_name: Weight-space composition algebra for combining ignition functions
supporting_evidence: S120-004 surveys weight-space operations; S120-002 connects attention to fast-weight programming; S120-009 shows hypernetworks can generate weights; S120-031, S120-035, and S120-036 route and compose LoRA adapters; S120-039, S120-045, and S120-046 perform averaging, arithmetic, and sign-aware merging in weight space.
non_supporting_evidence: Composition is empirical and heuristic. No source provides a formal algebra that guarantees the resulting weight artifact corresponds to a well-defined composition of the source functions. Model soups, task arithmetic, and adapter merging rely on geometric assumptions and are validated only by benchmark accuracy.
revised_assessment: GAP-016 has strong practical evidence but lacks formal algebraic grounding. Weight-space composition should be treated as an empirical approximation, not a strict function equivalence. Current confidence: MEDIUM.
readjudication_status_reason: Mapped from 121 partial/fulltext review to allowed status taxonomy.

gap_name: Equivalence checking across function representations (code, weights, spec)
supporting_evidence: S120-047 and S120-050 provide SMT-based equational reasoning for functional programs. S120-027 gives approximation theory for neural operators, which can be used to bound operator representation differences. S120-004 discusses comparing and embedding model weights.
non_supporting_evidence: No source provides a cross-representation equivalence checker (e.g., code vs. weights vs. spec). Neural operator approximation bounds are for PDE operators, not general functions. Weight-space similarity is behavioral/embedding-based, not semantic equivalence.
revised_assessment: GAP-017 is largely unsatisfied. The Function OS should not claim strict equivalence between code, weights, and specs without a dedicated verification layer. Current confidence: LOW.

gap_name: Effect tracking for side effects in function execution and composition
supporting_evidence: S120-053 and S120-055 provide algebraic effect handlers that separate effect signatures from their interpreters. S120-058 and S120-064 use effect handlers for probabilistic programming. S120-065 and S120-070 track and reuse agent skills whose executions have environmental side effects.
non_supporting_evidence: Effect handlers are language-level features and are not tied to neural function execution. Agent skill systems do not provide a formal effect calculus. The reviewed papers do not show effect tracking across code, weight, and spec representations.
revised_assessment: GAP-018 has a strong theoretical foundation in algebraic effects and practical motivation in agent skills. It requires integration into ignition's execution runtime. Current confidence: MEDIUM.
readjudication_status_reason: Mapped from 121 partial/fulltext review to allowed status taxonomy.

gap_name: Versioned registry of reusable ignition functions with provenance
supporting_evidence: S120-031, S120-035, and S120-036 manage pools of LoRA adapters with routing and merging. S120-039 and S120-045 collect and manipulate multiple fine-tuned checkpoints. S120-065 maintains a skill catalog with lifecycle and experience accumulation. S120-070 builds an ever-growing, automatically discovered, retrieved, and composed skill library.
non_supporting_evidence: None of these systems provide a unified, machine-verifiable provenance model across all representation types. Versioning is either implicit (adapter pools) or ad-hoc (skill libraries).
revised_assessment: GAP-019 is the most strongly supported by the reviewed full texts. The Function OS can build a versioned registry by combining adapter-pool and skill-library concepts. Current confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.

supporting_evidence: S120-058 introduces stochastic probabilities and nested inference for probabilistic programs. S120-059 gives operational and denotational semantics for higher-order probabilistic programming. S120-064 implements a universal PPL with composable effect handlers. S120-001 treats fuzzy functions as probabilistic/neural programs compiled into weights.
non_supporting_evidence: S120-001 is not a probabilistic programming language; it is a fuzzy-function compiler. The other sources do not connect probabilistic semantics to weight-space composition or neural network equivalence.
revised_assessment: GAP-020 has a strong theoretical and practical foundation in probabilistic programming. It can be layered onto ignition functions, but the connection to neural function composition is still an open research problem. Current confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.
